title: Native Java & Kotlin
objectives: Explain Kotlin's null safety and key features
Use data classes, extensions and scope functions

sections.markdown: Kotlin is the modern, official language for Android — concise, null-safe, and fully interoperable with Java. It compiles to the same JVM bytecode, so Kotlin and Java coexist in one project.

sections.code:
val name: String = "Ada"      // non-null
var nick: String? = null      // nullable
val len = nick?.length ?: 0   // safe call + Elvis
data class User(val id: Int, val name: String) // equals/hashCode/copy free
fun String.shout() = uppercase() + "!"          // extension function

rows: String vs String? checked by compiler

sections.markdown: Kotlin's null safety eliminates most NullPointerExceptions at compile time by separating nullable (String?) from non-nullable (String) types. This is the single biggest reason Google recommends Kotlin.
Overusing the !! (not-null assertion) operator — it throws an NPE if the value is null, defeating null safety. Prefer ?., ?:, and proper nullable types.

flashcards.back: The type system distinguishes nullable (T?) from non-null (T); the compiler enforces null checks.

flashcards.front: What does a data class generate?
flashcards.back: equals, hashCode, toString, copy, and componentN functions.
Both compile to JVM bytecode and call each other freely in the same project.
